title: Toward an evolutionary and syndromic psychiatry: Dogs as a comparative model for the neuroscience of psychopathology
title_zh: 迈向进化与综合精神病学：犬类作为精神病理学神经科学的比较模型
abstract: Psychiatric disorders arise from dysfunctions of neural systems that are deeply conserved across mammals, yet contemporary psychiatric classification remains fundamentally anthropocentric, relying heavily on subjective experience, symbolic language and self-report. This creates a major challenge for veterinarian psychiatrists and for comparative neuroscience: how can psychopathology be characterized across species when introspective access is unavailable? The domestic dog provides a uniquely powerful model for addressing this question, combining conserved affective and cognitive neural circuitry with species-specific socio-emotional adaptations shaped by domestication and exceptional phenotypic diversity generated by selective breeding. Here, we review the comparative neurobiology of cognitive and emotional regulation in dogs and humans, highlighting both shared neural architectures and critical species-specific differences in cognition, communication and social organization that limit direct transposition of human diagnostic categories. We then examine the principal methodological obstacles currently preventing canine psychiatry from becoming a mature neuroscience discipline, including the absence of standardized behavioral phenotyping, objective biomarkers, harmonized neuroimaging frameworks and operational diagnostic criteria. Building on recent advances in comparative neuroscience, evolutionary biology and dimensional psychiatry, we propose a species-centered syndromic framework in which canine psychopathology is defined through multidimensional profiles integrating behavior, physiology, neural circuits and developmental trajectories. This framework illustrates how comparative neuroscience can contribute to a broader evolutionary psychiatry, shifting psychiatric classification from language-dependent phenomenology toward biologically grounded, cross-species mechanisms of brain dysfunction. We argue that dogs are not merely translational models of human psychiatric disorders but a model system for developing an objective neuroscience of psychopathology.
abstract_zh: 精神障碍源于跨哺乳动物高度保守的神经系统功能失调，但当代精神病学分类仍以人类为中心，过度依赖主观体验、象征语言和自我报告。这为兽医精神病学和比较神经科学提出了重大挑战：在缺乏内省访问的情况下，如何跨物种表征精神病理学？家犬提供了一个独特而强大的模型，结合了保守的情感与认知神经回路以及由驯化和选择性育种产生的物种特异性社会情感适应和卓越的表型多样性。本文综述了犬类与人类在认知与情绪调节方面的比较神经生物学，强调了共享的神经结构以及在认知、交流和社会组织方面的关键物种差异，这些差异限制了人类诊断类别的直接迁移。随后，我们考察了目前阻碍犬类精神病学成为成熟神经科学学科的主要方法学障碍，包括缺乏标准化行为表型、客观生物标志物、统一的神经影像框架和可操作的诊断标准。基于最近在比较神经科学、进化生物学和维度精神病学方面的进展，我们提出了一个以物种为中心的综合框架，在该框架中，犬类精神病理学通过整合行为、生理、神经回路和发育轨迹的多维度特征来定义。该框架展示了比较神经科学如何为更广泛的进化精神病学做出贡献，将精神病学分类从依赖语言的现象学转向基于生物学、跨物种的脑功能失调机制。我们认为，犬类不仅是人类精神障碍的转化模型，更是开发客观精神病理学神经科学的模型系统。
